title: introduce-affordability-sweeper-batcher-and-quant-margin-estimator
author: Marisol Chen
release_notes: Introduces an automated affordability sweeper that proposes conservative batching/caching defaults for low-traffic tenants; introduces a quantization margin estimator that computes expected per-tenant cost/latency deltas and a risk score; adds econ-sweeper CLI with dry-run and apply modes; Console suggestions panel integration; rollout gated by opt-in and feature flag.
commits: init: add econ sweeper service skeleton and CLI entrypoint
feat(estimator): implement quant_margin estimator and risk scoring
chore: add conservative default batch/cache profiles and docs
test: integration tests and telemetry hooks; fix edge-case in KV cache rules
description: Context: Customers with many low-traffic tenants often pay a disproportionate fraction of token/unit costs because tenant defaults are conservative (large batch latency targets, no prefix caching, conservative quant profiles). This PR introduces two cooperating features: (1) an 'affordability sweeper' background job + CLI that scans tenant telemetry and suggests/apply conservative batching/caching defaults for tenants that meet opt-in heuristics, and (2) a 'quant-margin-estimator' that computes an expected per-tenant delta (cost, median latency, and a risk-of-regression score) when switching between quantization profiles. Motivation: shipping scalable cost optimization automation that is safe by default and auditable through Console suggestions. Design summary: - Sweeper runs as a low-priority background worker with two modes: dry-run (default) and apply. Dry-run populates suggestion records (Console suggestions API) and writes a preview manifest. Apply mode will create a change request for tenant defaults that requires team review and can be auto-approved for tenants flagged as low-risk. - Estimator uses sampled inference traces + micro-benchmarks (per-model, sequence-length buckets) to compute expected token cost delta and median latency change; it emits a conservative risk score combining historical P95 latency sensitivity and unit-econ variance. - Conservative default profiles are added under runtime/batcher/default_profiles.yaml and quant_profiles_v2.json; these are intentionally conservative (e.g., minimal-intensity batching, prefix KV caching ON for stable routes, prefer 4-bit quant with calibrated fallback) and annotated with the estimator's expected margins so operators can audit. Checklist: - [x] Sweeper service skeleton and CLI with dry-run - [x] Quant margin estimator core algorithm + unit tests - [x] Console suggestions integration (creates suggestion objects and preview manifests) - [x] Telemetry metrics for econ decisions (econ.sweeper.*) - [x] Integration tests for a simulated low-traffic tenant - [x] Feature flag behind configs/feature_flags.yaml (econ_sweeper.enabled=false by default) Implementation notes: - The sweeper is careful to only consider tenants with >72h of stable traffic and low unit-econ variance; opt-in is explicit (tenant_metadata.affordability_opt_in). - When in apply mode the system creates a staged change and posts a review link in the Console; we intentionally avoid automatic forced updates unless tenant marked auto_apply:true. - The estimator has two primary outputs: cost_delta_per_1k_tokens (USD), median_latency_ms_delta, regression_risk (low/medium/high). These are stored as suggestion metadata. Testing & CI: initial CI run failed on integration flakiness (KV cache timing), addressed by adding a small jitter and a deterministic mock for the micro-benchmark harness; final CI status: pass. Review summary: reviewers asked for additional safety checks (explicit tenant opt-in, add revert window, and per-tenant audit log entries). Those were implemented in commits 3/4. Rollout plan: - Merge behind feature flag; deploy sweeper as disabled by default. - Run sweeper in dry-run across canary region (eu-west-1) for 2 weeks and collect econ.sweeper.metrics. - If metrics stable, enable auto-suggestion publish for internal tenants; after pilot, enable apply mode for low-risk tenants. Migration & compatibility: No breaking API changes. Console suggestions are additive. Runtime default profiles ship as new YAML and are ignored unless referenced. Observability: new metrics and traces: econ.sweeper.suggestions_generated, econ.estimator.margin_samples, econ.apply.attempts, econ.apply.reverts. Rollback: feature flag off will prevent the sweeper from mutating tenant defaults; apply-mode changes are recorded and reversible via Console action. Related: ENG-8742 (tenant-affordability-pilot), ENG-8810 (quant-profile-regression-safety). Merge: squash and merge after approvals; merge commit SHA: d4b7f2a9.
